title: Stability liaison field kit and rapid escalation protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, field-friendly kit for reliability liaisons embedded with feature teams. The goal is to give non-SRE stakeholders the minimal tools, checklists, and escalation surface they need to detect, triage, and escalate issues that threaten SLOs (particularly P95/P99 latency and availability for inference endpoints) without burdening them with the full runbook library.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Stability liaisons (engineering leads), on-call product engineers, solutions engineers assisting customers, and SRE first responders.
- Systems in scope: Hosted API routing plane, model serving runtime, KV cache service, autoscaler, and data plane (ingest + inference).
- Out of scope: infra provisioning (cloud infra SRE), billing pipeline issues (finance-owned).

When to use this kit (triggers):
- SLO alert fired (availability or latency breach) and you are the on-call liaison.
- Customer reports reproducible degradation for a single route/model.
- Canary failing healthchecks > 3 consecutive windows.

Quick-reference contact ladder (rapid):
1) Liaison confirms impact and notifies #reliability-stability (Slack).
2) Ping primary on-call SRE (rotations > /oncall SRE list) and include short binder: route, model, region, timestamps, simple reproduction steps.
3) If primary SRE not responding in 8 minutes, escalate to SRE secondary and platform lead.
4) For customer-visible outages (tier 1 customers), escalate to Customer Success lead and on-call Solutions Engineer; include CS contact and customer org id.

Minimum telemetry snapshot to capture (first 10 min):
- Route + model id, request ids (sample up to 5 request IDs), timestamps.
- Tail latencies: P50/P95/P99 for the affected route over last 15 minutes (report numbers).
- Error classes: 5xx types, model-run timeouts, OOMs, kernel panic traces.
- Recent autoscaler adjustments (scale down/up events) and node replacement events in last 30m.
- Cache hit ratio for prefix/KV caches on the route.

Triage checklist (step-by-step):
1) Reproduce: run 3 synthetic requests to same route/model and note latencies and any error bodies. Keep one request id.
2) Check region routing: confirm the request is hitting intended region and variant (via request metadata). If misrouted, note routing policy that applied.
3) If latency spike without errors, inspect KV cache miss ratio and cold-start indicators (recent model swap, quantization toggle, new commit).
4) If errors present, copy error traces and correlate with recent deploys (deploy pipeline PR numbers).
5) Examine autoscaler logs for throttling or insufficient capacity decisions.
6) If GPU OOMs or kernel failures, capture node id and attach node logs; immediately tag SRE infra.

Rapid mitigations (short-lived):
- Route-level fallback: switch traffic to a lower-capacity model variant or older pinned version. Use canary window of 2–5% to verify.
- Soft degrade: enable response truncation to reduce token count for heavy requests if model runtime is the pressure point.
- Drain problematic nodes from pool if there are repeated OOMs; enable immediate replacement (fast-replace policy).
- Traffic shed: apply routing policy to drop low-value batch traffic for up to 10 minutes. Communicate to product owners.

Communication templates (Slack + incident channel starter):
- Subject line: [SLO ALERT] P99 latency breach - hosted-api / chat-generate / us-west1 - started 2027-04-02T09:13Z
- Message body: "TL;DR: P99 latency crossed 3s for chat-generate in us-west1. Affected customers: two PLG customers on default route. Current mitigation: shifted 10% traffic to model-v2-fallback. Next steps: collect synthetic traces, escalate to infra if OOMs. Liaison: Maya Chen. SRE on-call: Jordan Blake."
- Postmortem checklist link: paste link to PM template and mark owner.

Decision ladder (who can do what immediately):
- Liaison: can change routing policies for non-enterprise customers and request canary swap (<= 20% traffic).
- On-call SRE: can manipulate node pools, drain/replace nodes, and flip autoscaler thresholds for emergency window.
- Platform lead: can approve cross-region failover or emergency model rollback.
- CTO/VP Eng: required for customer communications if outage > 60 minutes or revenue impact > threshold.

Runbook snippets (copyable commands and checks):
- Check last 15m percentile: curl telemetry-api/internal/percentiles?route=chat-generate&window=15m --auth $TOKEN
- Sample request run: POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "x-route: chat-generate" -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' --record request-id
- Rotate fallback: api-cli rollout-route --route chat-generate --fallback-model model-v2-fallback --percent 10 --reason "latency emergency"
- Drain node: infrastructure-cli drain-node --node-id gke-usw1-node-123 --force --reason "OOM observed"

Cross-functional sprint plan (30-day phases, pragmatic):
- Week 0 (Prep): assign stability liaisons for 8 feature teams (names in linked sheet), share this kit, run 30m onboarding workshop.
- Week 1–2 (Experimentation): each liaison run 2 tabletop simulations using production-mirrored traffic; document gaps.
- Week 3 (Iterate): implement 3 highest-impact changes across platform (e.g., reduce autoscaler cooldown, add route-level cache warmup API, add synthetic canary suites).
- Week 4 (Harden): codify changes into one-page runbook snippets and roll into on-call rotation handbook.

Ownership & RACI (short):
- Liaison: detect, initial mitigation, customer communication until SRE takeover. (Responsible)
- On-call SRE: technical mitigation, node-level fixes. (Accountable)
- Platform Eng: implement fix PRs and config rollouts post-incident. (Consulted)
- Customer Success: external comms for customers flagged as impacted. (Informed)

Operational metrics to track in the next 90 days:
- Mean time to detection by liaison (target < 5 minutes after alert).
- Mean time to mitigation (target < 20 minutes for first mitigation).
- Fraction of SLO incidents mitigated by route fallback without infra change (goal 40%+).
- Number of tabletop rehearsals per liaison per quarter (goal 2).

Open questions & discussion items:
- What guardrails should we place around liaison-initiated autoscaler tweaks? (safety limits needed)
- Should liaisons be able to flip quantization/precision settings for model variants in emergency? Security/QA implications?
- Do we allow liaison-driven rolling restarts of model-serving pools or must SRE always perform?

Next immediate actions (owner + due date):
- Share kit in #reliability-stability and schedule the 30m onboarding workshop — Owner: Maya Chen — Due: 2027-04-06
- Create a short shared sheet listing liaisons and their coverage windows — Owner: Priya Rao — Due: 2027-04-08
- Add synthetic canary job for chat-generate route to CI (small QPS mimic) — Owner: Liam O'Neill — Due: 2027-04-14
- Draft limits for liaison changes to autoscaler thresholds and circulate for review — Owner: Jordan Blake — Due: 2027-04-10

Appendix: quick links and cheat codes:
- Slack channel: #reliability-stability
- Runbook source: https://go.redwood/runbooks/reliability
- Incident template: https://go.redwood/templates/incident-postmortem
- Liaison roster (temp): https://go.redwood/sheets/liaison-roster-2027-q2

Notes to self/TODOs (informal):
- Keep this doc short — the goal is frictionless adoption.
- Capture a handful of anonymized postmortem snippets to use as training examples in the onboarding workshop.
- Make a one-slide cheat-sheet for people to screenshot and carry on-call.

End of kit.
